questions.question: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working, what happens?

options.text: You will have no brakes at all.
You will still have brakes.
You should only use the parking brake to stop.
You should stop driving and wait for the ABS to work again.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS is added to your braking system to prevent brakes from locking during hard stops. If ABS fails, your regular brakes will still work. You can continue driving and braking normally.

questions.question: A convex mirror on the outside of a bus is adjusted correctly when:

options.text: You can see at least one traffic lane and the entire side of the bus.
You can see the front bumper.
You can see the top of the bus.
You can see the front windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see at least one traffic lane and the entire side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The outside mirrors on a school bus should show the front of the rear tires touching the ground, both sides of the bus, and at least one traffic lane on each side.

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Drive straight forward, then back to the right.
Drive straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Drive forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right maneuver, drive straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space lines.

questions.question: What do crossover mirrors help a school bus driver see?

options.text: The danger zones in front of the bus.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.
Vehicles in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zones in front of the bus.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help drivers see the danger zones directly in front of the bus and on both sides, from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: If you cannot find a student after they exit the bus, what should you do?

options.text: Secure the bus and look for the student.
Assume the student exited safely.
Walk to the back of the bus to check if they got back on.
Ask another student if they saw the missing student.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the bus and look for the student.
questions.explanation: If you cannot find a student after they exit, secure the bus and check around and under it for the missing student.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must always maintain ____ with the vehicle.

options.text: Three points of contact
Four points of contact
Two points of contact

questions.correctAnswerText: Three points of contact
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times when exiting. For buses, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can cause automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What condition should the drive shaft be in?

options.text: Bent toward the passenger side.
Bent toward the driver's side.
Bent to one side or the other.
Not bent.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not bent.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check that the drive shaft is not bent or cracked.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing in a placarded vehicle, you must always:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks in a placarded vehicle, stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, who decides if it is safe to cross?

options.text: Each driver decides for themselves.
A traffic control device decides.
Surrounding vehicles decide.
Passengers in each vehicle decide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each driver decides for themselves.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. Each driver is responsible for deciding when it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which of these is NOT required for the oil check?

options.text: Point out where the dipstick is located.
Show that the oil level is safe.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: You must show where the dipstick is, that the oil level is safe, and that it is above the refill mark. You do not need to show that oil is below the refill mark.

questions.question: When properly adjusted, school bus mirrors allow the driver to see ____ behind the bus.

options.text: 50 feet
100 feet
200 feet
1,000 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet
questions.explanation: Mirrors must be adjusted correctly for safe school bus operation. The flat mirrors should let the driver see 200 feet behind the bus. This is about four bus lengths.

questions.question: During a bus evacuation, students should be led at least ____ away from the road.

options.text: 10 feet
20 feet
50 feet
100 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: When evacuating a school bus, the driver must lead students at least 100 feet away from the road. This distance protects them from flying debris if another vehicle hits the bus.

questions.question: A bus driver should stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students because:

options.text: Students will walk to the bus, so the driver can see their movements better.
Buses are hard to drive.
Students might get scared when the bus comes toward them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students will walk to the bus, so the driver can see their movements better.
questions.explanation: Stop the school bus with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students. This makes students walk toward the bus. The driver can watch their movements more easily this way.

questions.question: If you must drive a school bus in reverse at a student pick-up point, you should:

options.text: Back up before students board the bus.
Back up after all students have boarded the bus.
Back up while students direct you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up after all students have boarded the bus.
questions.explanation: Backing up a school bus should only be done if there is no other safe way. If you must back up at a pick-up point, wait until all students have boarded first.

questions.question: What do outside crossover mirrors allow the driver to see?

options.text: The front bumper
The rear bumper
The right side of the bus
The left side of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The front bumper
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help the driver see the danger zone in front of the bus. They also show the danger zones on both sides of the bus, from the front to the service door.

questions.question: If there is a fire on a school bus, students:

options.text: Must leave the bus immediately.
Should stay on the bus but move away from the fire.
Should stay in their seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must leave the bus immediately.
questions.explanation: If a school bus is on fire or might catch fire, the driver must evacuate all students from the bus right away.

questions.question: If you must back up a school bus at a student pick-up point, you should:

options.text: Back up before students board the bus.
Let all students board the bus before backing up.
Let half the students board, then back up to meet the rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let all students board the bus before backing up.
questions.explanation: Do not put the school bus in reverse until all students have boarded. Always watch for students who arrive late.

questions.question: When alley docking, your first step should be to:

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: For alley docking, first drive past the alley and stop parallel to its outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley. Park in a straight line within the parking space.

questions.question: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks, students should:

options.text: Stay on the bus.
Get off the bus and stay near it.
Get off the bus and move far away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the bus and move far away from it.
questions.explanation: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks, evacuate everyone immediately. If a train hits the bus, lead students far away at an angle away from the tracks to avoid flying debris.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: Watch passengers.
See hazards on the road.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch passengers.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror in a school bus lets the driver monitor what passengers are doing inside the bus.
